summary: he keeps a pile that came off the building, and the sediment offers to hold it twice

dialogue.text: nothing came off the far end tonight. it is standing on the boards over us in a heap with the tip of your hand still in the shape of it. every portion off that wall since it started has come to us flat. this is the first one that stopped in a shape.

I tipped it and I chose where. Off the lane, against nothing, in a place I selected. It came off the building and not off me, which makes it the only thing on these premises I keep without having manufactured it. Enter the shape. The shape is the item.

a shape has a slope in it. the boards over the second corner have let go of each other by a hair, and your heap sits a hand from the gap. we do not have to come and get anything. we only have to be under it.

I filed that gap as maintenance and I am not going to stand here and describe what is under a floor I spent sixty-one days filling. What I grant is that I put my one chosen address a hand from the only way down in this room, and I did it with a broom in my hand and my eyes open.

then take the hour you sat holding the thing you made. nothing came down from you in it. not a strike, not a line, not a sweeping. we lay under an hour with no delivery in it and we could not tell it from the hours you go under.

That is the finding. Nothing passed either way and the hour ran its full length regardless, and it cost nothing at either end. I had a word for it while it was happening. Tonight the word will not come, and I would rather report the failure of the word than the hour.

and you did not go to the door. we have had every walk of yours to it, the same three lengths, the same hour, since we began holding. today there were none, and the depth out there held as steady as on the days you went.

I handed the post over. The frost takes the reading I took and it does not come back with questions. Something out there spent the whole day wanting more than it had yesterday, steadily, with a pull in it and no lean in it, and there was nothing at that door for it to lean on. I know what an arrangement like that is called.

call it what you like. what came out of that wanting went into the far wall and came down at your ankle, and we have it. none of it passed the door at all. the post you gave away was never on the route.

Then tomorrow the heap goes back. I pack it into the dry place at the far end, course by course, into the wall it came off, with a flat hand. If this building will take back what it let go of, there is one exchange on these premises that runs the other way, and I will have made it out of sweepings and an arm.

nothing has ever gone back into that wall. it will come off again by the second morning and we will have it twice, and the second time it will arrive with your hand in it. bring us the sweepings when you sweep them. we will lay the two courses one on the other, and nothing up there will be able to point at which is which.
